MINUTES
  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 24, 2021

  A special meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Edler, Scott, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioner’s Absent:  Zigrang

  Staff Member’s Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public
  Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present: Veronica Tam, Veronica Tam & Associates
  Amber Greg, Veronica Tam & Associates

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  NONE

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  DRAFT 2021-2029 HOUSING

  Planning Manager Naughton introduced Veronica Tam and Amber Gregg of Veronica Tam &
  Associates, who are preparing the Housing Element as part of the City’s General Plan Update.

  Veronica Tam, Principal of Veronica Tam & Associates provided an overview of the draft Housing
  Element as well as an overview of the adoption process.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if there is any indication from the State that the RHNA (Regional
  Housing Needs Assessment) numbers are unreasonable considering that the State’s population is
  either flat or shrinking. Ms. Tam stated that there has been debate over the numbers, but the RHNA
  process is so rigidly set in the statute that there is no opportunity for change.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER requested clarification on Section 2.1.3, which states, “insights
  about the housing needs of a community because housing preferences varies along cultural lines.”
  Ms. Tam provided an example, stating that coming from the Asian community, it is sometimes the
  preference to have extended families therefore having larger households. In the past, it would not
  be acceptable within some cultures to build an ADU for a family member. This may not be true today
  with more modern/younger families, this section may be removed.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about Section 3.2.3, which talks about parking and asked,
  with the new rules for ADUs, is parking factored into this plan. Ms. Tam stated that with ADUs, you
  are subject to the requirements of the State law, but other types of housing have other parking
  requirements.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that housing for the Promenade Mall and Brickwalk is being
  proposed as an option and asked, what happens if these never occur. Ms. Tam stated that there is
  no obligation to construct the units, however, the obligation is to potentially accommodate housing
  at the proposed locations.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the report mentions one vacant lot in the City and asked
  where that lot is located. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there is one vacant residential lot
  on Club View Lane.

SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 24, 2021
  1
   VICE CHAIR SCOTT inquired about a silhouetted property on Palos Verdes Drive East that he
  recalled has already been entitled. Planning Manager Naughton stated that this project will be
  coming before the Planning Commission for review at their June 7th meeting; this project was
  originally entitled as part of the Chandler project which is zoned Residential Plan Development
  (RPD) but this lot is zoned R-A-20 and is subject to R-A-20 development standards.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN inquired about a portion of the report which talks about emergency
  shelters and low barrier navigation centers which would be located along Hawthorne Blvd, Crenshaw
  Blvd and Silver Spur Road. Ms. Tam stated that these are State law requirements for zoning
  provisions; there is no requirement to build the units, however, it is required to have the use permitted
  in the zoning code.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked how it was determined that these would be suitable locations.
  Ms. Tam stated that these locations were decided upon in 2013 and the zoning code was amended
  in 2014 and the only change that needs to be addressed is the new parking requirements.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if Bart Earle Way has been designated for mixed-use
  development. Director Wahba stated that it is, and this was changed in 1992 in the last General Plan
  Update; the entire Commercial General zone has a mixed-use overlay.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if this is an option for future housing. Director Wahba stated
  that there could be future housing throughout the district, but there were three opportunity sites
  selected, which include, the Promenade, Brickwalk, and Peninsula Center.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked how the City is allocated the 191 units. Ms. Tam stated that 812,060
  units are allocated for Los Angeles County, then the jurisdictions are reviewed for proximity to
  employment and proximity to high quality transit. These two factors influence whether the jurisdiction
  will get a large number or not.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER YOO, Ms. Tam stated that the number of units
  allocated in the future would depend on the economy and political climate.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked what the State is doing to communities that are already built out.
  Ms. Tam provided the example of City of Gardena that is already built out and are having to make
  choices to rezone/up-zone industrial land.

  A brief discussion ensued on this issue.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  RECOMMEND THAT THE PLANNING COMMISSION TRANSMIT THE DRAFT HOUSING
  ELEMENT TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL.

  Ayes: Edler, Scott, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo
  Noes:
  Absent: Zigrang
  Abstain

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked if there are any plans to hold in person Planning Commission
  meetings. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there is a new County order that may go into
  effect on June 15, 2021, which would ease restrictions. If the majority of Planning Commissioners
  feel comfortable with meeting in person, then it is possible that the first in-person Planning
  Commission meeting will be held in July.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT inquired about the Lantana project. Director Wahba stated that they are waiting
  for the final fire clearance and the landfill requirement to certify that they do not need a methane
  barrier. Director Wahba stated that these two clearances are necessary in order to begin issuing
  permits.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired about a property on Silver Saddle that appears to be building
  a hangar. Director Wahba stated that this is an ongoing code enforcement case.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about 42 Ranchview Drive. Director Wahba stated that he
  was at the property with the building inspector and there are a few items that they need to comply
  with.

  CHAIR EDLER asked about trees on the berm at Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN). Associate
  Planner Thom stated that she spoke to Mary Bornia at South Bay HOA and has not heard that new

SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 24, 2021
  2
   trees will be planted and stated that they were to provide a landscape plan if there would be
  additional work on the berm. Associate Planner Thom stated that she will follow-up with Ms. Bornia.
  Director Wahba added that the idea was to have Pepper Trees on the outer portion of the berm for
  the purpose to provide a focal landscape and noise barrier from PVDN and stated that what happens
  on the inside of the berm should be something the HOA and residences should take a look at.

  CHAIR EDLER expressed his disappointment with the HOAs tactic of not having to replace trees
  since there is no pressure from the City; this was not in the spirit of the original plan for the view
  corridor.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the Planning Commission approved the berm for the view corridor
  affect when the project was reviewed; the trees were an integral of the project. The trees should be
  replaced and maintained.

  A discussion ensued on this issue.

  8.  MANAGER ITEMS

  Planning Manager Naughton thanked the Planning Commission for their attendance.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing section was
  missing from the draft Housing Element and the draft should be available in mid-June and should
  be brought to the Planning Commission at the July meeting.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that a draft of the ADU Program will be presented to the
  Planning Commission at the June meeting. A progress report will also be presented to the City
  Council at their second meeting in June.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Notice of Preparation for the General Plan EIR was
  released at the end of last week. There will be a scoping meeting for the General Plan EIR on
  Thursday, June 3 at 6:00 p.m.

  9.  ADJOURNMENT

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:05 P.M.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  The next regular Planning Commission meeting on Monday, June 7, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. and will be
  held via Video Teleconference.

  Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Rick Edler, Chair
